questions.q:
If for some x∈R, the frequency distribution of the marks obtained by 20 students in a test is:

Marks 2 3 5 7
Frequency distribution x+12 2x-5 x2-3x x

Then the mean of the marks is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Total students =20

⇒  x+12+2x-5+x2-3x+x=20

⇒   x2+2x+1+2x-5+x2-3x+x=20

⇒   2x2+2x-24=0  ⇒  x2+x-12=0

⇒    x=-4, 3    ∵  x>0

∴    x=3

Average =x+12×2+2x-53+5x2-3x+7×x20

=32+3+0+2120=2.8

Hence, required mean is 2.8

questions.q: Marks obtains by all the students of class 12 are presented in a freqency distribution with classes of equal width. Let the median of this grouped data be 14 with median class interval 12-18 and median class frequency 12 . If the number of students whose marks are less than 12 is 18 , then the total number of students is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { median }=\ell+\left(\frac{\frac{\mathrm{N}}{2}-\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{f}}\right) \times \mathrm{h} \\ & =12+\left(\frac{\frac{\mathrm{N}}{2}-18}{12}\right) \times 6=14 \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\frac{\frac{\mathrm{~N}}{2}-18}{12}\right) \times 6=2 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~N}}{2}-18=4 \Rightarrow \mathrm{~N}=44\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If the mean deviation about median for the number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>21</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>24</mn></math> arranged in the ascending order, is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn></math> then the median is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Median is the central value (or middle observation) of statistical data if it is arranged in ascending or descending order.

Thus, if there are n observations (variates) x1, x2, x3, …, xn arranged in ascending or descending order, then

median =n+12th observation, if n is odd

and median =n2 th observation +n2+1 th observation 2, if n is even.

Here we can see there are even number of terms,

So, median =2k+122=k+6

Mean deviation =∑xi-Mn=6

⇒k+3+k+1+k-1+6-k+6-k+10-k+15-k+18-k8=6

⇒ 58-2k8=6

⇒k=5

So, median =2×5+122=11

questions.q:
The frequency distribution of the age of students in a class of 40 students is given below.
$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|l|l|}
\hline \text{Age} & 15 & 16 & 17 & 18 & 19 & 20 \\
\hline \text{No of Students} & 5 & 8 & 5 & 12 & x & y \\
\hline
\end{array}$
If the mean deviation about the median is 1.25, then $4 x+5 y$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}=10 \ldots \ldots \ldots .(1) \\ & \text {Median }=18=\mathrm{M} \\ & \text {M.D. }=\frac{\sum \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{i}}\left|\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{M}\right|}{\sum \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{i}}} \\ & 1.25=\frac{36+\mathrm{x}+2 \mathrm{y}}{40} \\ & \mathrm{x}+2 \mathrm{y}=14 \ldots \ldots \ldots .(2) \\ & \text { by (1) & (2) } \\ & \mathrm{x}=6, \mathrm{y}=4 \\ & \Rightarrow 4 \mathrm{x}+5 \mathrm{y}=24+20=44\end{aligned}\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|}
\hline \operatorname{Age}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}\right) & \mathrm{f} & \left|\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{M}\right| & \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{i}}\left|\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{M}\right| \\
\hline 15 & 5 & 3 & 15 \\
\hline 16 & 8 & 2 & 16 \\
\hline 17 & 5 & 1 & 5 \\
\hline 18 & 12 & 0 & 0 \\
\hline 19 & \mathrm{x} & 1 & \mathrm{x} \\
\hline 20 & \mathrm{y} & 2 & 2 \mathrm{y} \\
\hline
\end{array}$

& \frac{\sum x_i}{6}=2 \text { and } \frac{\sum x_i^2}{N}-\mu^2=23 \\

questions.q: If the mean and the variance of $6,4, a, 8, b, 12,10$, 13 are 9 and 9.25 respectively, then $a+b+a b$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \because \text { mean }=9 \\ & \therefore 53+\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}=72 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}=19 \\ & \because \sigma^2=\frac{37}{4} \text { and }(\overline{\mathrm{X}})^2+\sigma^2=\frac{\sum \mathrm{x}_1^2}{\mathrm{~N}} \\ & \Rightarrow 81+\frac{37}{4}=\frac{529+\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2}{8} \\ & \Rightarrow 648+74=529+\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2=193 \\ & \because \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}=19 \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2+2 \mathrm{ab}=361 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{ab}=168 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{ab}=84 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{ab}=103\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
If the mean of the following probability distribution of a random variable $\mathrm{X}$ :
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline \mathrm{X} & 0 & 2 & 4 & 6 & 8 \\
\hline \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X}) & a & 2 a & a+b & 2 b & 3 b \\
\hline
\end{array}$
is $\frac{46}{9}$, then the variance of the distribution is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \sum P_i=1 \\ & a+2 a+a+b+2 b+3 b=1\end{aligned}4 a+6 b=1$ ...(I) $\mathrm{E}(\mathrm{x})=$ mean $=\frac{46}{9}\begin{aligned} & \sum P_i X_i=\frac{46}{9} \Rightarrow 4 a+4 a+4 b+12 b+24 b=\frac{46}{9} \\ & 8 a+40 b=\frac{46}{9}\end{aligned}4 a+20 b=\frac{23}{9}$ ...(II) Subtract (I) from (II) we get $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{b}=\frac{1}{9} \& \mathrm{a}=\frac{1}{12} \\ & \text { Variance }=\mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}{ }^2\right)-\mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)^2 \\ & \mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)^2=0^2 \times 9^2+2^2 \times 2 \mathrm{a}+4^2(\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b})+6^2(2 \mathrm{~b})+8^2(3 \mathrm{~b}) \\ & =24 \mathrm{a}+280 \mathrm{~b} \end{aligned}$
Put $\mathrm{a}=\frac{1}{12} \quad \mathrm{~b}=\frac{1}{9}\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^2\right)=2+\frac{280}{9}=\frac{298}{9} \\ & \therefore \sigma^2=\mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^2\right)-\mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)^2 \\ & =\frac{298}{9}-\left(\frac{46}{9}\right)^2 \\ & \sigma^2=\frac{298}{9}-\frac{2116}{81} \\ & =\frac{566}{81} \end{aligned}$

Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> is

questions.solution:

a1  be any natural number 

So, a1,a1+1,a1+2,….,a1+99 are values of ai or observation.

Now mean of the observation is given by,

x¯=a1+a1+1+a1+2+….+a1+99100

⇒x¯=100a1+(1+2+…..+99)100

⇒x¯=a1+99×1002×100

⇒x¯=a1+992

Mean deviation about mean=∑i=1100xi-x¯100

=2992+972+952+….+12100

questions.q: Let \(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{10}\) be ten observations such that \(\sum_{i=1}^{10}\left(x_i-2\right)=30, \sum_{i=1}^{10}\left(x_i-\beta\right)^2=98, \beta\gt2\), and their variance is \(\frac{4}{5}\). If \(\mu\) and \(\sigma^2\) are respectively the mean and the variance of \(2\left(x_1-1\right)+4 \beta\), \(2\left(x_2-1\right)+4 \beta, \ldots ., 2\left(x_{10}-1\right)+4 \beta\), then \(\frac{\beta \mu}{\sigma^2}\) is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \sum_{l=1}^{10}\left(x_l-2\right)=30 \\
& \sum_{i=1}^{10} x_l=50 \\
& \Rightarrow \text { Mean }=5 \\
& \text { Variance }=\frac{4}{5}=\frac{\sum x_l^2}{10}-(\bar{x})^2 \\
& \frac{4}{5}=\frac{\sum x_l^2}{10}-25 \\
& \Rightarrow \sum x_l^2=258
\end{aligned}$
Now, $\sum_{l=1}^{10}\left(x_l-\beta\right)^2=98\begin{aligned}
& \sum_{l=1}^{10} x_l^2-2 \beta \sum_{l=1}^{10} x_l+10 \beta^2=98 \\
& \Rightarrow 258-2 \beta(50)+10 \beta^2=98 \\
& \Rightarrow 10 \beta^2-100 \beta+160=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \beta^2-10 \beta+16=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \beta=8 \text { as } \beta \gt 2
\end{aligned}$
Now, as per the question
$2\left(x_1-1\right)+4 \beta, 2\left(x_2-1\right)+4 \beta, \ldots 2\left(x_{10}-1\right)+4 \beta$
Can be simplified as
$2 x_1+30,2 x_2+30, \ldots, 2 x_{10}+30\begin{aligned} & \mu=2(5)+30=40 \\ & \sigma^2=2^2\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)=\frac{16}{5} \\ & \frac{\beta \mu}{\sigma^2}=\frac{8 \times 40}{\frac{16}{5}}=100\end{aligned}$

& \text { mean }=\frac{\sum \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}}{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{8+21+\ldots+320}{25}=\frac{\frac{25}{2}(8+320)}{25} \\
